chunks: As for what Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā narrated from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Ṭalḥah ibn Zayd, from Jaʿfar, from his father, from ʿAlī عليه السلام, who said:
There is no harm in a boy who has not yet had a wet dream giving the adhān and leading the prayer.

So the proper way regarding this report is that we carry it upon one who is complete in intellect, even if he has not reached puberty; and the first report upon one in whom the conditions of legal responsibility have not been realized before reaching puberty, so that the two reports may be reconciled.

key_terms.الْغُلَامُ: a boy; here, a male child who has not yet reached puberty
key_terms.كَامِلَ الْعَقْلِ: fully mature in intellect and understanding
key_terms.يَؤُمَّ: to lead others in salat as Imam
key_terms.يَحْتَلِمْ: to experience a wet dream; used here as a sign of puberty

ai.seo_question: Can a boy who has not yet reached puberty give the adhān or lead the prayer in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith indicates that there is no objection to a boy who has not yet reached puberty giving the adhān and leading the prayer. The accompanying explanation reconciles this report with another by restricting it to a minor who is intellectually mature and possesses the qualities relevant to legal responsibility.
